questions.question: Which of the following is considered a strong password practice?
options: Using your birthday as the password
Using 'password123' for all accounts
Using a unique mix of uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols
Using your pet's name
questions.hint: Complexity and uniqueness make it harder for others to guess.

questions.question: What is 'phishing' in the context of data security?
options: Updating your software to the latest version
A trick to steal sensitive info via fake emails or websites
Storing your files in a cloud drive
Creating a backup of your computer
questions.hint: Think of it as 'fishing' for your private information using bait.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of enabling Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)?
options: It removes the need for a password
It makes the internet connection faster
It adds an extra layer of security beyond just a password
It automatically encrypts all files on your hard drive
questions.hint: It requires two different pieces of evidence to prove your identity.

questions.question: Under GDPR, what does the 'Right to Erasure' (Right to be Forgotten) allow individuals to do?
options: Delete their browser cookies
Request that an organization delete their personal data
Hide their profile from search engines
Change their legal name in government records
questions.hint: It focuses on the company's possession of your data.

questions.question: Which statement best describes End-to-End Encryption (E2EE)?
options: Data is encrypted only while it is stored on a server
The service provider holds the key to decrypt all messages
Only the communicating users can read the messages, not the service provider
Data is encrypted using a single password shared by all users
questions.hint: The encryption happens at the start and decryption happens only at the final destination.
